81241.subject: Progmat Moved $2.7 Billion to Avalanche. But What Actually Moved?
81241.body:
View this post on the web at https://www.team1.blog/p/progmat-moved-27-billion-to-avalanche

When Progmat completed its migration to Avalanche in July 2026, the headline number was ¥452 billion in digital securities, equivalent to roughly $2.7 billion at the time.
Progmat didn’t transfer $2.7B in cash; ¥452B is the total value of securities issued on its platform. That makes the migration less about capital moving between networks and more about changing the core technology underneath an operating financial market.
Progmat’s previous architecture was built on R3’s Corda 5, an enterprise distributed-ledger technology. It has since moved to a dedicated Avalanche L1, migrating its existing smart-contract functionality into an EVM-compatible environment while preserving the behaviour and specifications of existing issuances.
The transition was designed so participating institutions could continue using the platform without having to rebuild the financial products already running on it.
Want to keep up with the latest in the Avalanche ecosystem? Subscribe to the Team1 blog and get our updates in your inbox weekly.
The ¥452 billion did not “move” in the crypto sense
When Datachain announced the original migration plan in February, it described more than ¥439.6 billion in digital securities on Progmat ST. By the time the migration was completed, the figure reported by Avalanche had risen above ¥452 billion in total asset value.
For a crypto user, “moving assets to another chain” normally implies a transaction: burn here, mint there, bridge there, or transfer tokens from one wallet to another.
A tokenized bond remains connected to the underlying financial instrument and the legal rights associated with it. Changing the distributed ledger used to record and administer that instrument does not, by itself, change the bond.
The closer analogy is a financial institution modernizing its core technology while keeping its customer-facing services running. Commonwealth Bank of Australia, for example, has undertaken large-scale modernization of core banking infrastructure by moving critical systems to cloud infrastructure. Customers don’t need to understand the technology behind their accounts; the bank’s job is to upgrade it without disrupting reliable services.
That is the paradox of critical financial infrastructure: the more successful the migration, the less visible it can be.
Rebuilding the infrastructure underneath the securities
One of the more important pieces of the architecture is the mediation layer between Progmat’s applications and the underlying blockchain infrastructure.
Its purpose is to separate the financial services and business logic from the specific ledger supporting them. Rather than designing every application around one blockchain, Progmat can introduce an abstraction between its applications and the networks underneath them.

Good morning & happy Thursday! Today, we’re diving into Ramp’s bid for a national trust bank charter to see why the $60B fintech now wants to hold its customers’ money, not just track how they spend it (what the charter allows and what it doesn’t, the Stripe dependency it could remove, how its Vesto deal could pull corporate cash away from JPMorgan & BofA, & what to watch next + bonus deep dives into a16z’s State of Markets 2026: The AI Playbook for Founders and Investors [ https://substack.com/redirect/6e7b3c68-ddf3-47f5-aa49-3a4a22eb341c?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ], and How AI Agents Reshaped Jobs, Hiring and Productivity at Anthropic [ https://substack.com/redirect/079e532e-2fe1-4746-a32f-a556e39889df?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] inside), and breaking dow Claude Duet, Anthropic’s new always-on agent that arrived last to the AI agent race and still leaves OpenAI with the most to worry about (why it undercuts Dots at a fifth of the entry price while inheriting everything you’ve already built in Claude, why refusing to move money even with your approval is its real pitch to small businesses, & what’s next + bonus deep dives into Anthropic’s new IPO prospectus [ https://substack.com/redirect/778ad886-fdc8-45aa-85ef-56848c865e9d?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ]  [ https://substack.com/redirect/778ad886-fdc8-45aa-85ef-56848c865e9d?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ]& latest revenue numbers [ https://substack.com/redirect/778ad886-fdc8-45aa-85ef-56848c865e9d?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ], and How to Hire a Grok Bot: Your First AI Employee [ https://substack.com/redirect/e084e6db-7657-4270-88d8-72f5daa9f234?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] inside). So let’s jump straight into the finnovative stuff 🌶️
Ramp now wants to hold your company’s money, not just track it 🏦🤖
The news 🗞️ A week after launching Glass [ https://substack.com/redirect/d8afef8a-581c-457c-81f9-06ffcf2a02d5?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] to run its customers’ AI work, fintech giant Ramp has now asked federal regulators for a license to hold their money.

## AI found security flaws hiding in 70% of the web

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/778c44dd-6634-4f03-acb5-507e4041f55a/b20c7654-9b8a-426f-89c8-0418a3adc82f.jpg?t=1792657786)
Caption: 

Two critical security flaws had been hiding in PHP for more than a decade. [Wiz researchers revealed the vulnerabilities](https://www.wiz.io/blog/php2shell-php-rce) after working with OpenAI and PHP's security team to prepare emergency fixes.

PHP powers around 70% of websites, including platforms like WordPress and Drupal. The flaws, nicknamed **PHP2Shell**, could let attackers take control of vulnerable servers or access sensitive information.

* Both vulnerabilities received a critical severity score of 9.2 out of 10.

* Researchers used Google's Gemini 4 Argon, OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol, and Wiz Atlas to uncover and investigate the flaws.

* The coordinated disclosure gave PHP maintainers time to develop security patches before the vulnerabilities became public.

* Website operators running affected PHP versions are being urged to update immediately, as there is no complete workaround.

The discovery shows how AI is changing cybersecurity, helping researchers uncover hidden threats faster while potentially giving attackers access to similar capabilities.
